newsitem.title: THAILAND: Moody's says ratings gap may widen on Thai banks.
newsitem.headline: Moody's says ratings gap may widen on Thai banks.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said wide differences would continue to exist in the credit quality of Thai banks and the ratings gap may broaden between weaker and stronger institutions.

The ratings agency said in its annual report on the Thai banking system, obtained by Reuters on Wednesday, that the differences were due to tight liquidity, deteriorating asset quality trends and contingent liabilities.

"Financial fundamantals in many banks have been stressed in recent months by a likely economic slowdown, by problems in Thailand's property sector and by the financial crisis of confidence," Moody's said.

"Perhaps, some of the larger banks and finance companies (especially those affiliated with banks) benefited from the 'flight to quality' after the finance-company sector was subject to runs by depositors in February and March 1997," the report said.
But it said the high loan-to-deposit ratios of Thai banks and their reliance on short-term off-shore borrowings have significantly reduced their financial flexibility.
Moody's presently rates Thailand's foreign currency bonds at A3 and the rating of its banks' long-term deposits run from A3 for banks like Thai Farmers Bank to Baa3 for Bangkok Metropolitan Bank.
Late last month Moody's lowered its ratings on three medium-sized Thai banks including Bank of Ayudhya, Thai Military Bank and Siam City Bank.
Bank of Ayudhya's long-term senior debt and deposit ratings were lowered to Baa2 from Baa1. Long-term senior debt and deposit ratings of the two other banks were lowered to Baa3 from Baa2.
Also in April the agency downgraded the senior debt and deposit ratings of five major Thai banks to A3 from A2.
"It is Moody's view that asset quality trends will also remain negative for the medium terms," the agency said.

"Because of regulatory forbearance, however, Thai banks' economic reality (rising levels of delinquencies and non-performing assets) will not begin to be reflected fully in their publicly-disclosed levels of non-performing assets and financial statements until the second half of 1997," it said.

Moody's said it expected profitability for Thai banks to be under considerable pressure over the near term as the industry confronted the need to provision for, and charge-off, escalating levels of non-performing assets, particularly in the property sector.
